_note: V1.3g's content, and the only four verbs that write GameState.pacts and the chosen half of GameState.deployments. No terms ride these actions, unlike an agreement's multiplier or a measure's severity: a pact has no intensity, and a deployment's cost is DERIVED from the actor's military capability rather than authored -- which is the same cut tools/coercion_probe.gd made when it deleted tariff_rate_pct as one intensity written twice. See docs/defence-model.md.
_price_note: Every bloc_offset here is authored rather than left off, and that is V1.3f's correction applied in advance: the agenda's _act_domestic_price() reads this magnitude, so an act with no price at home is one the nine spend freely and forever. `settle_dispute` was 19 of the last 24 AI acts until the content started saying how hard each act was. 0.075 is the magnitude tools/diplomacy_probe.gd measured as moving one bloc's approval target 3.0 points, which is poll_noise.gd's NOISE_MAX_PCT.
_withdraw_note: withdraw_forces gates on deployment_chosen, NOT deployment_active, and that single word is why diplomacy_constants.PRECONDITION_FIELDS carries four defence pair fields instead of one. An obligation is not the player's to close -- only the aggressor lifting its measure, or abandoning the pact outright, can do that. On deployment_active this verb would hand the player a free exit from the one commitment the whole session exists to make them feel.

actions.name: Defensive Pact
actions.summary: A standing mutual defence commitment. If they are leaned on, you are in it -- and the bill arrives at home whether or not you agreed to that particular quarrel. Business reads it as stability; students read it as somebody else's war.

actions.name: Abandon the Pact
actions.summary: Walk away from the commitment, and from any forces standing under it. The obligation stops; so does the trust, and every nation with a stake in the ally you left takes their side.

actions.name: Deploy in Support
actions.summary: Send forces to stand with an ally, of your own accord. It costs a standing share of the budget for as long as they are there, and the country notices.

actions.name: Bring Them Home
actions.summary: End a deployment you chose to make. The budget line goes with it. A commitment an alliance obliged you into cannot be ended this way -- for that, there is only the pact itself.
